I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stay with the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That matches my land, my machinery, and the local water situation. At my age, I want a plan that is steady, practical, and not too risky. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is reliable and easier for me to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is worth it. I will keep fertilizer at moderate levels because I want stable output without wasting money. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, since wheat here usually needs more water support, especially around jointing and grain filling. I will use rotary tillage after harvest because it fits my equipment and saves labor, and I will keep pesticide use to a necessary level rather than spraying too often. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to keep a dependable harvest and manage costs and labor in a way I can handle myself.
